meta.purpose: User stories and acceptance criteria for the Calendaric rewrite. Acceptance criteria are the contract a building agent is validated against.

epics.title: Resolve, create, open and navigate periodic notes
epics.summary: NOTE owns the full lifecycle of a periodic note: knowing whether it exists, creating it (folder, template, file) when it does not, opening it the way the user asked, telling whether an arbitrary file is one of them, finding its neighbours, and keeping a fast index of all of it correct as the vault changes. FMT supplies date-to-filename and filename-to-date conversion and week/locale rules; TPL supplies what a template's tokens expand to; CAL and CMD decide when a note operation gets triggered (a click, a command, startup) and NOTE only supplies what happens once that decision is made; SET supplies the resolved folder/format/template values NOTE consumes.
notes: Every 'build' uid assigned to NOTE is covered by exactly one story's covers[]; none were left in uncovered[].

The generic create-note dispatcher's real defect (missing quarter/year branches, dni:create-periodic-note) is addressed as AC-NOTE-04.2/.3 rather than narrated as a bug: the entry point must handle every granularity Calendaric supports and report a clear error for one it does not.

Existing-file handling (AC-NOTE-04.5/.6) picks one answer where the old code had three (dni swallows the error behind a generic Notice and resolves undefined; pn lets vault.create's exception propagate unhandled; neither tells the caller anything actionable). The chosen answer: report the conflict clearly enough that the caller (typically US-NOTE-07's open-or-create) can recover by opening the existing note, and never destroy what is already on disk.

The vault-wide loose date-fallback (pn:loose-date-parsing-fallback-global) is icebox and intentionally excluded; AC-NOTE-08.2 and AC-NOTE-11.4 instead require folder-scoping as the only way a file is recognised as periodic.

Several stories (US-NOTE-03, 04, 05, 06, 07, 08, 09, 10, 11) are marked granularity-agnostic (day/week/month/year) even though Calendaric's own current code only wires day and week end-to-end; the underlying behaviour is already granularity-generic in the prior-art libraries (dni, pn), and quarter is the only granularity deliberately excluded (icebox). Wiring month/year all the way through settings UI and the calendar grid is CAL/SET/CMD/TPL's job, not NOTE's.

Most acceptance criteria are testable_by unit against a pre-populated index/cache and mocked vault calls; anything that touches a real Obsidian workspace leaf, a real vault.createFolder, or the confirmation modal is marked integration or (for the modal's own prompt) manual, since this epic's tests will need a fuller Obsidian mock (TFile, Vault, Workspace, MetadataCache) than exists in the current test suite.

pn:jump-to-adjacent-note-command and pn:open-adjacent-note-command are epic CMD, not NOTE: CMD's commands compose US-NOTE-09's closest-existing lookup and US-NOTE-07's open-or-create to implement 'jump to closest existing' and 'open the neighbouring date, creating it if needed' respectively. NOTE supplies both underlying operations; CMD decides how a command palette entry uses them.

epics.title: Filename formats, date parsing, week numbers, locale
epics.summary: This epic owns the two-way conversion between a date+granularity and a filename: generating a filename (including week tokens in the format field) from a date, and parsing an existing filename back into a date, deciding when that counts as a match. It also owns week numbering, week-start day, and locale, and validating a format string before it is saved. It hands NOTE the naming rules NOTE uses to look up, create and index files; NOTE decides what happens once a match (or collision) is found. It hands TPL the day-of-week resolution mechanism that TPL's note-body tokens also rely on, but owns only the filename-format-field half of the token syntax. SET owns where the format string lives and its settings UI; this epic owns only whether a given string is valid.
notes: Rival implementation decision: US-FMT-04 adopts the 'try every candidate format' structure (the one that already expands nested-path formats into a full-path and a basename-only candidate), because that structure is required anyway to support nested folder formats. Layered on top, it keeps the week-number-vs-month/day disambiguation from the single-format implementation, but applies it consistently to both the exact-match and the prefix-match branch, fixing an inconsistency present in the old single-format implementation (which only disambiguated on its exact-match branch). The undecided residue (candidate tie-break order, and how narrowly the disambiguation rule is scoped) is listed in US-FMT-04's open_questions.

pn:loose-date-parsing-fallback-global (a vault-wide loose date guess when no configured format matches at all) is icebox, not part of this epic; US-FMT-04's failure paths intentionally stop at 'not recognised' rather than falling back to a global guess.

forks:weekly-note-prefix-match and forks:periodic-note-prefix-match-setting describe the same prefix-matching feature family as pn:strict-then-prefix-date-parsing and pn:allow-prefix-match-gate, just observed from the other historical codebase; they are folded into the same story (US-FMT-04) rather than duplicated into a second one.

Most acceptance criteria in this epic are unit-testable in isolation (pure date math), which is why testable_by is almost always 'unit' rather than 'integration' or 'manual'; the two 'integration' criteria in US-FMT-04 are the ones that assert against the real shape of the user's existing vault, and the one 'manual' criterion in US-FMT-03 covers a live-reload UX check that is hard to assert purely in a unit test.

SET owns the settings UI for the format field, the prefix-match toggle, and the locale/week-start dropdowns; this epic owns only what those stored values must cause to happen. NOTE owns what happens once a note is found or not found (create, open, index); this epic only decides whether a given filename counts as a match. TPL owns the same {{weekday:fmt}} token syntax inside the note body; this epic owns only its use inside the filename format field, sharing the day-of-week resolution mechanism (dni:get-day-of-week-numerical-value) with TPL as a cross-epic dependency rather than a duplicated rule.

epics.title: Template files and token substitution in the note body
epics.summary: This epic owns turning a loaded template's raw content into the text a new note actually contains: substituting {{date}}, {{time}}, {{title}}, day-relative and weekday tokens, leaving anything it does not recognise untouched, and validating that a configured template path is usable. It does not create the file or decide when a template is applied (NOTE), does not touch the same token syntax used in the filename Format field (FMT), and does not store the template path setting (SET). Because every real template in this vault hands the interesting work to a full template engine instead of using these tokens, roughly half of this epic's stories pin down the boundary with that engine rather than the tokens themselves.
notes: None of the 13 vault:* evidence templates actually use this plugin's own {{...}} tokens; they implement the same ideas (dates, weekday headings, prev/next links) directly in Templater scripts and hand off renaming, moving, and even creating another note to Templater. That makes the composability and ordering boundary (US-TPL-05, US-TPL-06) the load-bearing requirement of this epic in practice, not the token set itself.

US-TPL-03 documents a real, already-observed defect (see calendaric-map.json observations, severity P2, 'docs/guide.md ... vs formatWithWeekTokens/applyWeekTokens hard-code ISO weekday numbering'): the same {{weekday:fmt}} syntax is implemented once and shared between the note body (this epic, applyWeekTokens) and the filename Format field (FMT, formatWithWeekTokens calls the same helper). Fixing one without the other reintroduces the mismatch the observation already flagged.

Most stories are unit-testable in isolation (pure string substitution over a date and a config). US-TPL-05 and part of US-TPL-06 are the exception: verifying that a second, independently installed plugin observes the right content and does not get fought requires either an integration harness with a real template-engine plugin or a manual check — flagged per-criterion as 'integration' or 'manual'.

epics.title: The calendar view: grid, navigation, indicators, interaction
epics.summary: This epic owns everything the user sees and clicks inside the calendar view itself: the month grid (including adjacent-month days and the week-number column), moving between months and back to today, the click/modifier-click/hover/right-click behaviour of every cell type (day, week number, month header), the indicator dots on a cell and the detail shown for them, and keeping all of that current as files, settings, the active note, and the clock change. It boundaries against NOTE (which owns actually opening or creating a note file), CMD (which owns the command/ribbon that opens this view), SET (which owns the settings values themselves, not the view's reaction to them) and FMT (which owns the week-number value, not its display column).
notes: Almost every acceptance criterion in this epic is DOM/interaction-driven (click, hover, contextmenu, live vault events) and is only testable_by 'manual' or 'integration'. The exceptions are pure grid/date math and word-count-to-dot-fill logic (US-CAL-01, most of US-CAL-07), which are testable_by 'unit'.

US-CAL-03, US-CAL-04 and US-CAL-05 depend on NOTE's 'open or create a note for a date' capability and on FMT's/SET's resolution of where and how that note is named; this epic owns only the click/hover/menu request that triggers it and the resulting view-level effect (which pane, whether the grid navigates), never the file operation itself. Exact NOTE story IDs were not guessed and are left out of depends_on.

The conflict between 'open the month note' and 'reset to today' on the month header is resolved in US-CAL-05: the header always tries to open/create the displayed month's note when monthly notes are available, and only falls back to resetting to today when they are not. Returning to today on demand (when monthly notes ARE available) has its own separate, always-present control, covered in US-CAL-02, so the two gestures never compete for the same click.

The vault's real-world indicator is the word-count dot (US-CAL-07); the streak, tags and tasks indicator sources seen in the old plugin are in the icebox (epic ICE) and are intentionally not covered here. US-CAL-07's multi-source acceptance criterion (AC-CAL-07.4) keeps the door open for the icebox sources, or any other future source, without naming an interface.

pn:text-input-suggest-popper-positioning (US-CAL-12) is mapped from a settings text-input autocomplete in the source plugins, but is written here as the generic overlay-positioning behaviour this epic's own hover popover (US-CAL-08) needs; whether it ends up as one shared mechanism with SET's inputs or a duplicated implementation is flagged as an open question rather than assumed.

epics.title: Configuration model and settings UI
epics.summary: SET owns the shape of Calendaric's configuration (what is stored per granularity versus what is global), the settings screen that edits it, persisting it safely across restarts and hand-edits, and the guarantee that a saved change reaches the rest of the plugin without restarting Obsidian. It stops at the boundary of what a value means: FMT decides whether a format string is valid, TPL decides what a template does, NOTE decides how a folder is used to create a note, and MIG owns importing configuration from other plugins and upgrading old stored shapes — SET owns the field that holds each of those values and the feedback shown when a value is rejected.
notes: Of the 80 mapped settings-map rows, most are the SAME logical field recorded once per source plugin (dni, cal, pn, calendaric, vault, forks); they do not each need a distinct key in the new model. Concluded canonical survivors: 6 per-granularity fields (enabled, format, folder, templatePath, openAtStartup, allowPrefixMatch) for day/week/month/year, plus roughly 7 global fields (week start, show week numbers, confirm-before-create, locale override, words-per-dot, the single implicit configuration group, and the internal daily-notes-import-shown flag).

Dropped as explicitly dead (stored and editable but never read by anything, per the map's own notes): cal's weeklyNoteFormat/weeklyNoteTemplate/weeklyNoteFolder, pn's hasMigratedDailyNoteSettings, hasMigratedWeeklyNoteSettings, installedVersion, and pn's dead-duplicate ISettings localeOverride/weekStart fields. AC-SET-06.5 asserts none of these come back.

Dropped as icebox-scoped, not because they are wrong: every quarterly-granularity row (periodic-notes.settings.quarterly.*, the vault's calendarSets[].quarter, and the placeholder Monthly/Quarterly/Yearly UI groups), enableTimelineComplication, and calendar-set plurality (activeCalendarSet as a user-facing choice). The underlying array/id may still exist internally as the single implicit group's id; it is just never exposed as a choice.

Collapsed as duplicate multi-source read paths now replaced by one source of truth (US-SET-03): daily-notes.format/folder/template (core plugin copy), calendar.options.weeklyNoteFormat/Folder/Template (legacy Calendar-plugin copy), and every periodic-notes.settings.<granularity>.enabled 'use Periodic Notes settings' precedence flag — with a single stored value per field there is nothing left to choose between.

Out of SET's scope entirely: app.vault.getConfig('weekStart') and ('localeOverride') read Obsidian's own vault-wide config rather than a Calendaric-owned key, and Templater's templates_folder/trigger_on_file_creation_mode/folder_templates and the core daily-notes.json format belong to the plugins MIG imports from, not to Calendaric's own configuration shape.

Roughly a third of the acceptance criteria in this epic are testable_by manual or integration rather than unit, because the behaviour under test is either a live settings-screen interaction (inline validation feedback, the guide link) or requires the calendar view and command palette to observe reactivity end to end.

US-SET-04 and US-SET-06 reference 'invalid stored data' and 'the format/folder/template check fails' without asserting what specifically makes a value invalid — that judgment belongs to FMT (format), NOTE (folder) and TPL (template); this epic only owns that the field shows the feedback and that saving still succeeds.

uncovered.reason: This is the breadcrumb router that moved the settings screen between a calendar-set list page and a calendar-set detail page. With calendar sets in the icebox and exactly one implicit configuration group (US-SET-01), the settings screen has one page and nothing to navigate between; the router's own behaviour (for example that it always resets to the dashboard on close) has no equivalent to carry forward.

epics.title: Commands, ribbon, menus and startup behaviour
epics.summary: This epic owns every way to reach a periodic note without opening the calendar view first: the command palette, the ribbon icon and its context menu, and automatic note-opening at vault startup. It also owns the calendar view's own entry point (opening and auto-revealing it) and reveal-in-calendar shortcuts. It does not own what a note operation actually does when triggered (NOTE), the calendar view's own grid and interactions once open (CAL), or which granularities are enabled and which note is configured to open at startup (SET) - it only owns how the command surface reacts to those choices.
notes: Every build uid assigned to CMD is covered by a story; nothing was folded into 'uncovered'.

Most acceptance criteria in this epic need Obsidian's workspace, command and hotkey APIs to observe (testable_by: integration), because the epic is almost entirely about entry points into the host application rather than pure logic. The exceptions are the two per-command id-stability criteria in US-CMD-05 (snapshot-testable as plain string comparisons) and the startup-exclusivity criterion in US-CMD-09 (a pure settings transform, already unit-tested in one source plugin).

US-CMD-06 and US-CMD-07 are written as separate stories on purpose: 'jump' never creates a note and reports when there is nothing to jump to, while 'open next/previous' always succeeds by creating the note. Their acceptance criteria show this contrast rather than stating it as a cross-command comparison.

Commands that call into note creation or lookup (US-CMD-04, US-CMD-06, US-CMD-07, US-CMD-08, US-CMD-09) treat that creation/lookup as a black box owned by NOTE; this epic's criteria only cover whether the command is offered, and what the user sees at the entry point, not how the note itself is built.

epics.title: Importing existing configuration and coexisting with other plugins
epics.summary: This epic gets an existing user's configuration into Calendaric's own shape: reading it out of the core Daily Notes plugin, the Calendar plugin and the Periodic Notes plugin, offering it as a reviewable, reversible import rather than a silent overwrite, and turning off the plugins it replaces only with consent. It also covers noticing when one of those plugins is still active so Calendaric does not fight it, and keeping Calendaric's own stored configuration loadable across its own version changes. It stops short of defining the target configuration shape (SET) and recognising notes already on disk (NOTE/FMT).
notes: The real disagreement between periodic-notes-anks's stale top-level 'monthly' key and its live calendarSets[0].month value (folder '_00 Planer/_03a Miesiące Work' / template 'Monthly work.md' vs. the correct '_00 Planer/_03 Miesiące' / 'Monthly Periodic Template.md') is recorded in calendaric-map.json as an observation, not as a capability, so it has no uid to cite in constrained_by. AC-MIG-04.2 encodes it directly.

Three of the fifteen build capabilities in this slice (cal:daily-notes-plugin-warning-banner, pn:getting-started-banner-daily-notes-detection) are UI banners best exercised manually; most of the rest need a real Obsidian plugin instance to test meaningfully, so this epic leans integration/manual rather than unit.

No predecessor plugin ever imported the Calendar plugin's or the Periodic Notes plugin's configuration into another plugin's settings -- only the Daily Notes import path (calendaric:import-daily-notes-settings) existed before. US-MIG-03 and US-MIG-04's Periodic-Notes-facing half, and all of US-MIG-07, are therefore new behaviour with no old capability to point to in 'covers'.

Cross-plugin detection by plugin id is still needed for the three named predecessor plugins (core Daily Notes, Calendar, Periodic Notes) to drive imports and the coexistence notice in US-MIG-06 -- see that story's open_questions for why the old dev/production dual-id probe specifically should not carry forward.

epics.title: Architecture, boundaries, testability and release quality
epics.summary: This epic defines the architectural skeleton the other epics build inside: what layers exist, which way dependencies may point, what must be provable by a test without Obsidian running, and what a release must guarantee before it ships. Its boundary with the other epics is that it never describes user-visible behaviour itself — it constrains how the behaviour described elsewhere is allowed to be built, tested, documented and shipped.
notes: The two capability uids assigned to ARCH (forks:settings-tab-crash-guard-1.13, forks:git-dependency-self-build) are both single-defect fixes; every other criterion in this epic is derived directly from observations in calendaric-map.json rather than from a capability, per the schema's allowance for observation-derived criteria with covers left empty.

US-ARCH-05 (extensibility) and parts of US-ARCH-06 (release quality) are marked testable_by "manual" because verifying them means actually attempting the exercise (add a granularity, add an indicator, break a tooling gate) and reviewing the result's shape, not running an existing automated check.

tsconfig.json today enables several individual strict-family flags (noImplicitAny, noImplicitThis, strictNullChecks, strictBindCallApply, useUnknownInCatchVariables) but never sets the single "strict": true option, so it is missing others from that family (e.g. strictFunctionTypes, strictPropertyInitialization) implicitly. AC-ARCH-04.1 is written against the single-setting requirement rather than naming which flags are currently absent, since that list would go stale as the config changes.
No vault:* evidence-role capabilities were assigned to ARCH in epic-assignment.json, so no story carries a constrained_by entry.

stories.title: Look up whether a period already has a note
stories.story: As someone reviewing my periodic notes, I want to check whether a note for a specific day, week, month, or year already exists, so that other features can decide whether to open it or create it without guessing.
stories.rationale: Every open-or-create flow, calendar dot, and adjacent-note search depends on this lookup being fast and correct.

acceptance_criteria.given: a note exists for the requested period
acceptance_criteria.when: the lookup runs for that period
then: the existing note's file is returned

acceptance_criteria.given: no note exists for the requested period
acceptance_criteria.when: the lookup runs for that period
then: the lookup reports nothing found
no note is created as a side effect of looking
no error is thrown

acceptance_criteria.given: two moments that fall on the same day, week, month, or year but differ only in time of day
acceptance_criteria.when: the lookup runs for either moment
then: both return the same note

acceptance_criteria.given: a granularity Calendaric does not support (for example quarter)
acceptance_criteria.when: a lookup is requested for it
then: a clear, actionable error is reported instead of an incorrect or silent result

stories.title: Enumerate every note of a granularity
stories.story: As someone auditing my notes, I want to list every note of a given granularity that exists in the vault, so that calendars, dashboards, and migrations can be built on a complete set instead of a partial guess.
stories.rationale: Calendar dots, related-note lists, and index rebuilding all need the complete set, not a sample.

acceptance_criteria.given: notes exist at several dates for a granularity, including some nested in subfolders under its configured folder
acceptance_criteria.when: notes of that granularity are enumerated
then: every one of them is returned, including the nested ones

acceptance_criteria.given: the granularity's configured folder does not exist in the vault
acceptance_criteria.when: notes of that granularity are enumerated
then: a clear error is reported naming the missing folder, instead of an empty list that looks like there are simply no notes yet

acceptance_criteria.given: the granularity's configured folder exists but is empty
acceptance_criteria.when: notes of that granularity are enumerated
then: an empty list is returned without an error

acceptance_criteria.given: a file in the configured folder does not match the granularity's configured filename format
acceptance_criteria.when: notes of that granularity are enumerated
then: that file is excluded from the results

stories.title: Resolve the folder for a note and create missing parent folders
stories.story: As someone who has never manually created a folder for my notes, I want the plugin to create whatever folders a new note needs, so that turning on a granularity or pointing it at a new folder just works without a manual setup step.
stories.rationale: A missing folder should never be the reason a note fails to be created.

acceptance_criteria.given: a granularity's configured folder does not exist yet
acceptance_criteria.when: a note is created for that granularity
then: the folder, and any missing parent folders above it, are created automatically before the note is written

acceptance_criteria.given: no folder is configured for a granularity
acceptance_criteria.when: the path for its note is resolved
then: the note falls back to Obsidian's own default location for new notes, rather than an unpredictable or empty path

acceptance_criteria.given: a configured folder path that is empty or the vault root
acceptance_criteria.when: the folder path is checked for validity
then: it is accepted as valid

acceptance_criteria.given: a configured folder path that does not currently exist in the vault
acceptance_criteria.when: the folder path is checked for validity ahead of note creation
then: it is flagged as not-yet-created
the flag does not block a note from being created later, since the folder is made automatically at creation time

acceptance_criteria.given: a configured folder several levels deep where none of the intermediate segments exist
acceptance_criteria.when: a note is created for that granularity
then: every missing intermediate folder is created, not only the immediate parent

stories.title: Create the note for any supported granularity, reliably
stories.story: As someone keeping a periodic journal, I want creating a note to work the same reliable way for every granularity Calendaric supports, so that switching between daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly notes never surprises me with a create that silently does nothing or crashes.
stories.rationale: The old code has three different, inconsistent answers for what happens when a create goes wrong; users need one predictable answer.
open_questions: Is a bare 'create' ever invoked directly by another epic, or does every real entry point go through open-or-create (US-NOTE-07), which already checks existence first? This changes how often AC-NOTE-04.5/.6 are actually reachable in practice.

acceptance_criteria.given: no note exists yet for the requested period
acceptance_criteria.when: a create is requested for that period
then: a new note file is written at the resolved folder and filename for that granularity
the created file is returned to the caller

acceptance_criteria.given: a granularity Calendaric currently supports (day, week, month, or year)
acceptance_criteria.when: the generic 'create the note for this granularity' entry point is used
then: it creates the note correctly for that granularity, the same as calling that granularity's own create operation directly

acceptance_criteria.given: a granularity Calendaric does not support (for example quarter)
acceptance_criteria.when: the generic 'create the note for this granularity' entry point is used
then: a clear, actionable error is reported naming the unsupported granularity, instead of an internal or unhandled failure

acceptance_criteria.given: the configured folder for the granularity does not exist yet
then: the note is still created successfully
the missing folder is created automatically first

acceptance_criteria.given: a file already exists at the exact path a new note for this period would be written to
acceptance_criteria.when: a create is requested for that period
then: no existing content is overwritten or deleted
the operation reports clearly that a note already exists there, instead of silently doing nothing or throwing an unhandled error
the caller can use that report to open the existing note instead

acceptance_criteria.given: the exact path a new note would occupy is taken by something that is not a markdown note (for example a folder)
acceptance_criteria.when: a create is requested for that period
then: the create fails with a clear, actionable error naming the conflict
nothing at that path is altered or deleted

stories.title: Apply the configured template when creating a note
stories.story: As someone with a note-taking routine, I want each newly created periodic note to start from my configured template, so that I do not have to add the same headings and frontmatter by hand every time.
stories.rationale: A template is the difference between a useful note and a blank file; it must apply every time a note is created, not just sometimes.

acceptance_criteria.given: a template is configured for the granularity
then: the template's content, with its tokens expanded, becomes the new note's initial content

acceptance_criteria.given: no template is configured for the granularity
then: the note is created with empty content rather than failing

acceptance_criteria.given: the configured template file cannot be found
then: the note is still created, with empty content
a specific, visible warning tells the user the template could not be read

acceptance_criteria.given: a saved fold state exists for the configured template
acceptance_criteria.when: a new note is created from it
then: that fold state is applied to the new note

stories.title: Open a note in the active pane, a new tab, or a split
stories.story: As someone jumping between notes quickly, I want opening a note to reuse my current view by default but let me force a new tab or a split when I ask for it, so that navigating never fights the layout I already have open.
stories.rationale: Where a note opens is as much a part of the experience as whether it opens at all.

acceptance_criteria.given: a note is opened without any modifier key held
then: it reuses the current unpinned tab instead of opening a new one

acceptance_criteria.given: a note is opened while the platform's split modifier key (Cmd on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere) is held
then: it opens in a split next to the current view instead of replacing it

acceptance_criteria.given: a note is opened as part of the startup flow rather than a direct user click
then: it opens in a new tab rather than reusing or replacing whatever tab is already active

acceptance_criteria.given: the resolved file was deleted or moved between being found and being opened
then: a clear notice is shown
no unrelated file is opened in its place

stories.title: Activating a period opens or creates its note
stories.story: As someone keeping a periodic journal, I want activating a period to take me straight to its note, so that I never have to manually find or create the file myself.
stories.rationale: This is the single most-used operation in the plugin: the payoff every other NOTE story exists to support.

acceptance_criteria.given: no note exists for the activated period
then: a note is created for it
the newly created note opens

acceptance_criteria.given: a note already exists for the activated period
then: the existing note opens
no duplicate is created and its content is left unchanged

acceptance_criteria.given: the setting to confirm before creating is turned on and no note exists for the activated period
then: the user is asked to confirm before any file is written
declining the confirmation creates nothing and opens nothing

acceptance_criteria.given: the setting to confirm before creating is turned off and no note exists for the activated period
then: the note is created and opened immediately, without any prompt

acceptance_criteria.given: creating the note for the activated period fails
then: a clear, actionable error is shown
no blank or broken pane is left open in place of a real note

stories.title: Know whether a file is a periodic note, and which period
stories.story: As someone who wants navigation commands to only apply where they make sense, I want the plugin to tell whether any given file is one of my periodic notes and, if so, which period it represents, so that features like jump-to-adjacent only ever activate for real periodic notes.
stories.rationale: Every command that only makes sense on a periodic note needs a precise, folder-scoped answer to 'is this one?'.

acceptance_criteria.given: a file sits inside a granularity's configured folder and matches its configured format
then: it is recognised as a periodic note of that granularity
the exact period it represents is returned

acceptance_criteria.given: a file's name looks like a date but the file does not live inside any granularity's configured folder
then: it is not recognised as a periodic note

acceptance_criteria.given: a file is not a markdown file
then: it is never recognised as a periodic note, regardless of its name

acceptance_criteria.given: a file was previously recognised as a period's note and is then renamed without changing which period it represents
then: it is still recognised as the same period's note

stories.title: Find the closest existing adjacent note
stories.story: As someone reviewing my history, I want to jump to the closest existing note before or after the one I am looking at, without creating anything new, so that I can browse what I have actually written without accidentally adding empty notes.
stories.rationale: Browsing history and filling in a missing day are two different intents and must not be conflated.

acceptance_criteria.given: at least one earlier note and one later note of the same granularity exist relative to a reference note
acceptance_criteria.when: the previous, or the next, adjacent note is requested
then: the nearest existing note in that direction is returned

acceptance_criteria.given: no earlier, or no later, note of that granularity exists
acceptance_criteria.when: the previous, or the next, adjacent note is requested in the direction with nothing there
then: nothing is returned, instead of an error or a result wrapped around to the other end

acceptance_criteria.given: the reference file is not itself a recognised periodic note
acceptance_criteria.when: an adjacent note is requested from it
then: nothing is returned, since there is no period to be adjacent to

acceptance_criteria.given: the neighbouring date for the requested direction has no note yet
acceptance_criteria.when: the closest existing adjacent note is requested
then: no note is created for that neighbouring date

stories.title: Week-relative tokens in the filename format follow the configured week start
stories.story: As someone naming weekly notes with per-weekday tokens, I want {{monday:DD.MM}} and its six siblings to resolve to the date that falls in my own configured week rather than a fixed Monday-first week, so that the filename always names the days of the week I actually see everywhere else in the plugin.

stories.title: Month and week layout follow the configured week start
stories.story: As someone viewing a month of notes, I want each week's row to start on my configured week-start day and always show a complete 6-week grid, so that the week numbers and day columns match how I think about weeks.

stories.title: Locale and week-start settings govern weekday names and week numbers everywhere, live

stories.title: Parse a filename back into a date, honouring nested folders and an opt-in prefix fallback
stories.story: As someone who already has years of periodic notes on disk, I want the plugin to recognise which date and granularity each filename represents, even when the note lives in a dated subfolder or carries an extra descriptive suffix, so that my existing notes keep working after I switch to this plugin.
stories.rationale: Two independent old implementations of this exact behaviour exist and disagree; this story is the single specification the rewrite must follow so an existing vault keeps recognising its own notes.
open_questions: Between the two old implementations, one tries only the single format resolved for the requested granularity, the other tries every candidate format (full path and basename-only) for that granularity. This story adopts the every-candidate-format approach so nested-path formats work, and requires the strict-then-prefix decision below; the remaining open point is the tie-break order when more than one candidate format produces a valid match for the same file — today's code always takes the first candidate in an unspecified list order, and this story does not change that.

Should the week-number-vs-month/day disambiguation described in AC-FMT-04.5 also apply when a format has a day token but no month token, or only when both a month and a day token are present, as in the narrower of the two old implementations?

acceptance_criteria.given: a granularity's configured format contains a folder separator, such as a year folder followed by a full date

acceptance_criteria.when: the plugin resolves notes for that granularity
then: the file is still recognised, matched against its filename alone rather than its full path

acceptance_criteria.given: a filename does not exactly match the configured format for a granularity, but starts with what that format would produce for some date, followed by extra descriptive text

acceptance_criteria.given: the same filename and format as AC-FMT-04.3, but prefix matching is enabled for that granularity
acceptance_criteria.when: the plugin resolves notes for that granularity
then: the file is recognised as a note for that date, as an inexact (prefix) match rather than an exact one

acceptance_criteria.given: a weekly format includes both a week-number token and a month or day token
acceptance_criteria.when: a filename is parsed against that format, whether the eventual match is exact or a prefix match
then: the week number encoded in the filename takes priority over any conflicting month or day fragment
this priority is applied the same way regardless of whether the match found is exact or a prefix match

acceptance_criteria.given: the vault already contains 219 daily notes named in the pattern "YYYY-MM-DD, dddd", 60 weekly notes named "YYYY-Wnn, DD.MM - DD.MM", 21 monthly notes named "YYYY-MM Month", and 25 monthly-work notes named "YYYY-MM Month - Work"

acceptance_criteria.when: the plugin looks up the note for that period

stories.title: Canonical identity for a date and granularity
stories.story: As the system matching notes and calendar cells to periods, I want a single date and granularity to always produce the same canonical identity, so that two references to "this week" or "this day" are recognised as the same period regardless of the exact time of day carried by the underlying date value.

acceptance_criteria.given: no granularity is specified when requesting an identity

then: it is recognised as that week's note

then: no identity is returned, and the file is not treated as a periodic note for either granularity

stories.title: Fill date, time, and title tokens into the template body
stories.story: As someone applying a template to a new periodic note, I want {{date}}, {{date:FORMAT}}, {{time}}, {{title}}, and date-arithmetic tokens like {{date+1d:FORMAT}} filled in automatically, so that the note already carries the right day, time, and name without me typing them by hand.

stories.title: Fill {{yesterday}} and {{tomorrow}} into daily note templates only
stories.story: As someone journaling day by day, I want {{yesterday}} and {{tomorrow}} in a daily note's template to resolve to the adjacent calendar days, so that I can link into my journal's timeline without typing dates.
stories.rationale: This is a daily-only convenience carried over from the source plugins; the rewrite should keep the asymmetry explicit rather than silently extending or dropping it.

acceptance_criteria.given: a daily note's template contains {{yesterday}}
then: it is replaced with the calendar day before the note's own date

stories.title: Fill named weekday tokens into a weekly note's template body, honouring the configured week start
stories.story: As someone whose weekly template lays out one heading per day, I want {{monday:FORMAT}} through {{sunday:FORMAT}} to resolve to the correct calendar date for that weekday of my own week, so that the headings are right whether my week starts on Monday or on Sunday.
stories.rationale: The current implementation hard-codes an ISO Monday-start week for this token family, so it silently produces the wrong date whenever the configured week start is not Monday; this pins the correct rule down before the bug is carried into the rewrite.
open_questions: The Sunday-first rule in AC-TPL-03.2 is derived from the token's own definition, not observed in this vault: every real template here, including the weekday-header generator this story is constrained by, assumes an ISO Monday-first week. then: it is left in the note exactly as written

stories.title: Validate that a configured template path resolves to a usable file
stories.story: As someone configuring which file a granularity's notes are templated from, I want to be told when that path does not point at a real, readable file, so that I find out at configuration time rather than the first time a note is created with an unexpectedly empty or broken body.

then: it operates on the note's current name and location

acceptance_criteria.given: a template's own logic decides to leave the note empty or unchanged because its own internal validation failed, independent of this plugin

acceptance_criteria.given: no external template engine is installed or configured at all

stories.story: As a Calendaric user reading the format-and-template guide, I want every behaviour it documents to match what the plugin actually does, so that I can trust the documentation instead of discovering the real behaviour by trial and error.
stories.rationale: The map found docs/guide.md stating that week tokens follow the user's configured week-start setting, while the code that resolves those tokens hard-codes ISO week numbering regardless of that setting — the documented and the implemented behaviour disagree today.
open_questions: Which behaviour is correct for week-based template tokens: ISO week numbering, or the user's configured "Start week on" setting? The map found the guide and the code disagree; deciding which one is right is a product decision this epic cannot make on its own.

acceptance_criteria.given: a behaviour described in the user-facing guide
then: a test asserts the documented behaviour directly
the guide and the code cannot silently diverge without a test failing

acceptance_criteria.given: the guide states that week-based template tokens follow the "Start week on" setting
acceptance_criteria.when: a week-based template token is resolved
then: it uses the day configured in "Start week on", not a fixed numbering independent of that setting
if fixed numbering is kept instead, the guide's wording is corrected to describe that behaviour accurately

acceptance_criteria.given: the guide is opened from within the plugin's settings
then: it works on every platform the manifest declares support for
opening the guide does not depend on a desktop-only capability when the manifest declares mobile support

acceptance_criteria.given: a documented setting, command, or behaviour is renamed, removed, or changed
then: the guide is updated in the same change
it is not left for a later, separate pass

icebox.title: Quarterly notes
icebox.what_it_does: Adds a fifth note granularity, quarter, with the same create, look-up, enumerate, and settings-resolution behaviour that day, week, month and year already get: a user could open or create 'this quarter's note' from a configured folder, format and template, and the plugin would detect whether quarter notes are turned on. It would also replace today's dead 'Quarterly Notes' and 'Custom Notes' rows in Settings, which currently render as permanently-disabled, unclickable headings, with a real working section or remove them entirely.
icebox.why_deferred: The user has quarter notes switched off in her live configuration, with no folder or template ever set for them, so nothing in the vault depends on this granularity existing.
evidence: vault: calendarSets[0].quarter has enabled=false, format='YYYY-[Q]Q', folder='', templatePath='' in the live periodic-notes-anks config — quarter is disabled and unconfigured

map: calendaric's own settings UI already ships a 'Quarterly Notes' toggle row that is permanently disabled with no expandable content, and 'Custom Notes' has no backing data shape anywhere in the codebase at all — both were UI scaffolding for a feature that was never wired up
icebox.cost_rationale: Month and year notes are being built in this release with the same create/get/enumerate/resolve-settings shape quarter would need; once that generic per-granularity machinery exists, adding quarter mostly means adding one more entry to a config list and one more format/folder/template settings row, not new architecture.
blocks_if_omitted: NOTE epic: the note-granularity code (create, get, enumerate, resolve-settings, and the generic create-note dispatcher) must be written as one function per operation driven by a granularity list, not five hand-written copies or a switch statement naming day/week/month/year explicitly — otherwise adding quarter later means touching every one of those functions instead of extending a list.
SET epic: the per-granularity settings model and settings-UI row renderer must already be generic over 'whichever granularities exist' so a quarter row can be added without a new UI component.
icebox.revisit_when: The user turns quarter notes on in her own settings, or starts wanting a genuine quarterly review note distinct from the existing Templater-driven '_04 1on1' folder, which already covers a quarterly-ish cadence entirely outside this plugin.
icebox.risk_of_deferring: Nothing — no current note, template, or workflow depends on quarter notes existing.

icebox.title: Multiple calendar sets
icebox.what_it_does: Lets a user maintain more than one independent bundle of day/week/month/quarter/year settings — for example a 'Personal' set and a separate 'Work' set with their own folders, formats and templates — and switch which one is active from a command, a fuzzy-search quick-switch modal, or a settings dashboard listing every set as a card with add, duplicate, rename and delete controls plus a details page per set.
icebox.why_deferred: The user's live configuration defines exactly one calendar set ('Default'), and her actual Personal/Work split is already handled a different way: a second physical folder, a separate template, and a ' - Work' filename suffix, not this plugin's calendar-set mechanism. There is no observed need for a second set.
evidence: vault: activeCalendarSet is 'Default' and only one calendar set exists in the live periodic-notes-anks config — multi-calendar-set support is unused

vault: the Work vs personal split in this vault is implemented ad hoc via a second folder, a separate template, and a ' - Work' filename suffix, not via periodic-notes' own multi-calendar-set mechanism — a merge should not assume calendar sets are how 'Work' is actually kept separate here
icebox.cost_rationale: The CRUD UI (dashboard cards, a details page per set, inline rename, duplicate/delete with a last-set guard) and the switch-time side effects (re-run command and ribbon registration, reset the note cache) are a real chunk of settings-UI and state work on top of whatever the single-set v1 already builds — but only additive UI, not a data migration, provided the underlying config is already array-shaped (see blocks_if_omitted).
blocks_if_omitted: SET epic: the settings data model must store configuration as an array of calendar sets plus an 'active set' pointer (CalendarSet[] + activeCalendarSet), even though v1 only ever creates one set automatically — never as a single flat per-granularity settings object. Storing it flat now means a real data migration is needed the day a second set is added.

NOTE and CAL epics: every place that resolves 'the' folder, format or template for a granularity must resolve it through 'the active calendar set', not a hardcoded single settings reference, so switching sets later changes behaviour everywhere automatically instead of requiring each call site to be found and rewritten.
icebox.revisit_when: The user wants a genuinely separate calendar configuration — different active granularities, formats or folders per context — rather than today's folder-plus-suffix convention, for example if she takes on a second, unrelated vault-like context inside the same vault.
icebox.risk_of_deferring: If the SET epic's first release hard-codes a single implicit set instead of an array, adding calendar sets later becomes a migration of every existing user's settings JSON rather than a feature switch-on. This is the one item in this icebox where the architecture choice made now has a real, avoidable later cost.

icebox.title: Extra calendar indicator (dot) sources
icebox.what_it_does: Adds three more kinds of small indicator dots under calendar days and weeks, beyond the word-count dot already being built: a plain has-a-note dot, a dot coloured or labelled from the note's frontmatter tags, and an unfilled dot when a note has incomplete task checkboxes — plus a workspace event other installed plugins could listen to in order to register their own indicator sources.
icebox.why_deferred: The only dot source actually configured anywhere in the vault is the word-count-based one; no tag-based, task-based or streak-based indicator is set up in any readable plugin config, so nothing today shows a user has ever turned on or missed these.
evidence: vault: the Calendar plugin's word-count-based heatmap dot (wordsPerDot) is the only dot source configured; no custom or metadata-based dot source appears in any readable config
icebox.cost_rationale: If CAL epic's day-metadata resolution is built as a list of pluggable sources, even with only word-count shipped in v1, each of these three is a small, self-contained function of the same shape — a cheap store lookup for streak, a metadata-cache read for tags, a cached file read plus regex for tasks — and the third-party extension point is a thin wrapper over the same list.
blocks_if_omitted: CAL epic: the 'resolve per-day/week metadata' architecture story should keep the per-cell dot pipeline as an ordered list of source providers, not a single hardcoded word-count code path, so streak, tags, tasks and third-party sources can be added as new list entries later without restructuring how dots are rendered.
icebox.revisit_when: The user starts using frontmatter tags or task checkboxes as a way to mark a day's status she wants visible at a glance on the calendar, or installs a third-party plugin that wants to contribute its own indicator.
icebox.risk_of_deferring: Nothing — no workflow today reads, or would notice the absence of, these dots.

icebox.title: Timeline complication
icebox.what_it_does: Shows a small floating badge in the corner of any open periodic note with a relative-date label such as 'Today' or 'Last week' (plus an arrow if the note was only an inexact match); clicking it expands into a 7-day strip for jumping to a nearby day without leaving the note. It would mount and unmount itself automatically as markdown panes are opened and closed.
icebox.why_deferred: The user's live configuration has this feature's toggle turned on, but nothing in her actual templates, dataview queries or note content references or uses a timeline view — the setting is on, but the feature it promises has never been exercised.
evidence: vault: enableTimelineComplication=true in the live periodic-notes-anks config, but no template, dataview query, or note content in the readable vault references a timeline view — enabled but unused
icebox.cost_rationale: It needs its own mount/unmount lifecycle manager reacting to workspace layout-change events across every open leaf, plus a small interactive UI component and the relative-date-formatting helper it depends on — a self-contained vertical slice, bounded but not trivial.
icebox.revisit_when: The user notices she wants faster day-to-day navigation from inside an already-open note without returning to the calendar view, or the 'enabled but does nothing' mismatch in her own config prompts an explicit decision either way.
icebox.risk_of_deferring: Nothing — today the setting is a switch that promises a feature nobody has built or missed.

icebox.title: Related-files and natural-language date switchers
icebox.what_it_does: Lets a user type a free-text date query — 'next monday', 'in 3 weeks', 'last month' — into a modal and jump straight to that period's note; pressing Tab hands off to a second list of every cached note related to that period, optionally including finer granularities, for example every daily note inside a chosen month.
icebox.why_deferred: This whole capability only activates when the third-party nldates-obsidian plugin is installed, and the vault's confirmed list of enabled community plugins does not include it — building this today would ship a command that never appears.
evidence: vault: community-plugins.json's confirmed enabled list is calendar-anks and periodic-notes-anks only — nldates-obsidian is absent
map: pn:nl-date-navigator only registers its command when app.plugins.getPlugin('nldates-obsidian') exists — the whole capability is inert without that plugin installed
icebox.cost_rationale: The source material itself flags the hand-off between the two modals — closing one, opening the other, replaying the typed query via a synthetic input event — as untested, fragile glue, and its keyboard shortcut reaches into an unexposed, undocumented Obsidian modal internal (the private `chooser` field); building this well means redesigning that hand-off, not porting it as-is.
blocks_if_omitted: NOTE epic: keep a callable 'list every cached note for a period, optionally at finer granularities' lookup (the get-periodic-notes-related behaviour) as part of the note-lookup API even though no UI calls it in v1 — both this switcher and any future one would depend on it existing.
icebox.revisit_when: The user installs and starts relying on nldates-obsidian for other purposes, or specifically wants free-text date entry as an alternative to the calendar grid.
icebox.risk_of_deferring: Minor — grid-based navigation still gets her to any date; this is a convenience layer that today would depend on a plugin she doesn't run.

icebox.title: Drag-and-drop note dragging
icebox.what_it_does: Lets a user drag a day, week, or month cell's note out of the calendar view — for example to drop its link into another note, or the file itself onto another pane — using the operating system's native drag gesture.
icebox.why_deferred: The only way to implement this relies on an untyped, undocumented Obsidian internal (app.dragManager) rather than any stable, public Obsidian API, and no vault evidence shows this interaction being used or needed.
evidence: map: calui:drag-day-or-week-note depends on an untyped, undocumented Obsidian internal (app.dragManager) — a fragile external dependency, not a stable API
map: dragging a cell with no existing file still starts a drag with the file undefined, with behaviour then entirely dependent on that internal's own undocumented handling
icebox.cost_rationale: Correctness depends on an Obsidian-internal API that can change without notice across Obsidian releases, unlike every other cell interaction (click, hover, context-menu) in the CAL epic, which use documented public APIs — this one needs its own ongoing compatibility watch regardless of when it is built.
icebox.revisit_when: Obsidian publishes a documented drag-and-drop API for file links, or the user specifically asks to drag a periodic note's cell into another note or pane.
icebox.risk_of_deferring: Nothing lost by waiting — and building it earlier would not remove the ongoing risk of it breaking silently on an Obsidian upgrade, since that risk comes from the API it depends on, not from when it is built.

icebox.title: Vault-wide loose date parsing fallback
icebox.what_it_does: When no calendar set's configured folder-and-format matches a file, the old code falls back to guessing a date from the bare filename anywhere in the vault, using a loose regex for a YYYY-MM-DD-ish, YYYY-MM-ish, or bare 4-digit-year substring, and treats any match as if it were a periodic note.
icebox.why_deferred: This is a defect, not a postponed feature. The fallback is not scoped to any calendar set's configured folder, so any markdown file anywhere in the vault whose name merely contains a year, month or day-shaped substring gets miscached as an inexact periodic-note match. It should not be carried into the rewrite in this form.
evidence: map (P2 bug): 'the vault-wide loose date-fallback in cache.resolve() is not scoped to any calendar set's configured folder... any markdown file anywhere in the vault whose basename merely contains a YYYY-MM-DD/YYYY-MM/YYYY-shaped substring (e.g. "2026 Meeting Notes.md") gets cached as an inexact match for every calendar set that has active granularities, which can surface as incorrect +N related notes badges and pollute the related-files switcher with unrelated files'
icebox.cost_rationale: If a scoped version is ever wanted, it is a small change: restrict the same regex fallback to run only inside a calendar set's own configured folder, reusing the strict-then-prefix matching FMT and NOTE are already building instead of inventing a new mechanism.
blocks_if_omitted: FMT epic: the date-parsing and note-resolution stories must not include a vault-wide, unscoped loose-match fallback; any 'last-resort' filename guess must be scoped to a calendar set's configured folder from the start, so this bug is not reintroduced by accident during the rewrite.
icebox.revisit_when: Never in its current unscoped form. Revisit only if there is a real request for a folder-scoped loose-match fallback as a genuinely new, bounded feature — at which point it should be designed fresh against FMT's real parsing rules, not ported from this code.
icebox.risk_of_deferring: None — leaving this out removes a source of miscategorized notes; no value is lost by not rebuilding it.

excused.reason: This is the breadcrumb router that moved the settings screen between a calendar-set list page and a calendar-set detail page. With calendar sets in the icebox and exactly one implicit configuration group (US-SET-01), the settings screen has one page and nothing to navigate between; the router's own behaviour (for example that it always resets to the dashboard on close) has no equivalent to carry forward.
